mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility has risen steadily for three consecutive weeks (-45.1 to -36.1), indicating resumed commuting and lunchtime/after-work footfall near employment hubs, which mechanically lifts retail and recreation visits over the following four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -45.1 to -36.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is not higher than the prior 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing to rise each week.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility improves by more than 5 points week-on-week, it signals a relaxation of movement restrictions that enables non-essential travel to shopping and leisure destinations, raising RETAIL_REC within two weeks of the transit jump.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -58.7 to -48.4 over the snapshot window, with a 9.1-point jump between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of a TRANSIT week-on-week improvement exceeding 5 points, or declines instead.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve simultaneously for two consecutive weeks, commuting and errand-running combine to compound retail footfall gains beyond what either series predicts alone, producing a reinforcing four-week uplift in RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved in every week of the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is no larger than the sum of growth predicted from WORKPLACES and TRANSIT taken independently, or RETAIL_REC falls despite joint improvement.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined for three straight weeks (-4.9 to -14.3) consistent with shortening daylight and cooling temperatures reducing outdoor recreation; this seasonal substitution effect redirects leisure activity toward indoor retail and recreation venues, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -4.9 to -14.3 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days even as PARKS mobility continues its downward trend across the same period.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC's week-on-week gains have sharply decelerated, from +19.4 points (t-2w to t-1w) to +1.0 point (t-1w to t-0w), indicating the reopening rebound is saturating; if this deceleration persists for two consecutive weeks it signals an approaching plateau or reversal rather than continued strong growth.
candidate_trigger: week-on-week RETAIL_REC change falls below 2 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC week-on-week change dropped from +19.4 to +1.0 between the last two observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC resumes growth of more than 5 points week-on-week within the next 1-2 weeks despite the observed deceleration.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized near -11 to -12 points after earlier declines, suggesting essential-shopping demand has normalized; as essential trips plateau, discretionary spending and trips shift toward retail and recreation categories, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved only from -12.7 to -11.4 in the last two weeks, a near-plateau
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM remains flat or continues to recover.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has fallen from 18.6 to 13.7, indicating people are spending less time confined at home; once RESIDENTIAL drops below a 15-point threshold it reflects a durable shift to out-of-home activity patterns, including retail visits, within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell to 13.7 at t-0w, crossing below 15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks after RESIDENTIAL drops below 15 points, or RESIDENTIAL reverses upward while RETAIL_REC still rises.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of declining PARKS mobility and rising TRANSIT mobility signals a seasonal regime shift where outdoor leisure is being replaced by transit-enabled indoor retail trips; this interaction amplifies RETAIL_REC growth beyond either trend alone over a four-week horizon, but only during the autumn/winter transition period.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines while TRANSIT simultaneously improves for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -4.9 to -14.3 while TRANSIT rose from -58.7 to -48.4 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is no greater than what PARKS or TRANSIT trends alone would predict, or RETAIL_REC declines despite the joint pattern continuing.
